fall_protection.official_text: Employees on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge 6 feet or more above a lower level must be protected by guardrails, safety nets, or personal fall-arrest systems.
fall_protection.interpretation: Primary broad fall card for roof edges, floor edges, platforms, formwork, elevated decks, and other raised walking/working surfaces. Retrieval terms include fall hazard, height, elevated work, unprotected edge, guardrail, harness, lanyard, lifeline, and lower level.
fall_protection.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly working on, standing beside, climbing to, or moving along an elevated edge, open side, platform, roof, formwork, raised deck, or similar location with a lower level or credible fall path.
fall_protection.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project fall-protection concern when Pass 1 clearly establishes elevated-edge or opening exposure and the relevant protection is explicitly Not visible or visibly inadequate. Do not discard a clear Pass 1 elevated-exposure finding merely because an exact 6-foot measurement cannot be read from a still image; state that the statutory height threshold is not measurable when necessary. Use Possible concern only when the image does not establish an edge/opening exposure or the protection status is Unclear.
fall_protection.uncertainty_policy: Do not invent exact height, full edge coverage outside the frame, an anchor point, or a harness connection. If the worker, the fall path, or the control is hidden or blurred, retain the observed cue but report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
fall_protection.consistency_rule: Never call a guardrail, safety net, harness, lanyard, lifeline, anchor, cover, or barrier absent if Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

fall_opening_protection.official_text: Employees on walking/working surfaces shall be protected from falling through holes by personal fall-arrest systems, covers, or guardrail systems erected around the hole.
fall_opening_protection.interpretation: Use specifically for floor holes, skylights, shaft openings, stairwells, elevator openings, slab voids, and uncovered penetrations. It gives retrieval a direct opening/shaft/skylight vocabulary instead of relying on the broad edge card.
fall_opening_protection.visual_trigger: A person is visibly beside, over, stepping around, or working adjacent to an uncovered floor opening, shaft, stairwell, skylight, slab penetration, or similar hole.
fall_opening_protection.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project fall concern when an opening and the exposed worker are clearly visible and no cover, guardrail, or other evident protection separates the worker from the opening. Do not require an exact opening dimension when the fall path is visually obvious. If a cover or rail may exist outside the crop, use Possible concern rather than declaring it absent.
fall_opening_protection.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer that a dark area is a hole, that a cover is unsecured, or that a worker is exposed when their position relative to the opening is unclear.
fall_opening_protection.consistency_rule: Preserve any Pass 1 observation of a cover, guardrail, toe-board, barrier, harness, lanyard, or edge protection.

fall_arrest_system.official_text: Personal fall-arrest systems must meet the criteria in 29 CFR 1926.502(d) when they are used to meet fall-protection requirements.
fall_arrest_system.interpretation: Use for a worker visibly relying on a body harness, lanyard, lifeline, anchor, or personal fall-arrest system at height. A harness alone is not proof of protection; the connection and appropriate anchor/line must be visible or otherwise reported as Not assessable.
fall_arrest_system.visual_trigger: A worker at a fall-exposure location is visibly wearing a harness, or a harness/lanyard/lifeline is visibly present near the worker.
fall_arrest_system.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a fall-arrest concern when Pass 1 clearly shows a worker exposed at height wearing a harness but the lanyard is explicitly Not visible, visibly disconnected, or visibly attached to an unsuitable location, and no guardrail or other fall-protection alternative is visible. Do not downgrade a disconnected-lanyard observation merely because the exact height cannot be measured.
fall_arrest_system.uncertainty_policy: If the lanyard connection, anchor, or complete fall-protection system is outside the frame, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable rather than assuming disconnection.
fall_arrest_system.consistency_rule: A harness, lanyard, lifeline, anchor, guardrail, or safety net recorded as Visible or Unclear must not be re-described as absent.

scaffold_safety.official_text: Each employee on a scaffold more than 10 feet above a lower level must be protected from falling; scaffolds must also be inspected and used safely.
scaffold_safety.interpretation: Use for scaffold platforms, mobile scaffolds, suspended scaffolds, temporary work platforms, scaffold access, missing guardrails, unsafe platform edges, and visibly defective or overloaded scaffold conditions.
scaffold_safety.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly on, climbing, accessing, erecting, dismantling, or working from a scaffold or temporary scaffold platform.
scaffold_safety.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project scaffold-safety concern when the image clearly shows a worker on a scaffold with an open side/end, missing/ineffective visible guardrail, unsafe access method, visibly broken platform component, or another direct scaffold cue. Do not require the exact 10-foot measurement to preserve a clear scaffold fall cue; report that statutory height is not measurable if needed. Use Possible concern when the scaffold height or protection coverage cannot be judged.
scaffold_safety.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer scaffold load rating, inspection status, full platform decking, or complete rail coverage from a partial image.
scaffold_safety.consistency_rule: Do not call a guardrail, toe-board, ladder, platform, brace, harness, or lanyard absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

ladder_safety.official_text: Portable ladders used to access an upper landing surface must extend at least 3 feet above it or be secured with a grasping device; non-self-supporting ladders must be used at an appropriate angle and on stable surfaces unless secured.
ladder_safety.interpretation: Use for portable ladders, leaning ladders, stepladders, ladder access to roofs/scaffolds, unstable placement, missing landing extension, and workers overreaching or using obviously unsafe ladder positions.
ladder_safety.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly climbing, standing on, working from, or accessing an elevated surface with a portable or fixed ladder.
ladder_safety.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project ladder-safety concern only for a direct visible cue: ladder base on unstable/slippery support, ladder visibly unsecured and displaced, worker standing on an obviously prohibited top position, missing visible landing extension with no securing/grasping arrangement, or unsafe ladder angle clearly apparent. Do not confirm solely because a ladder is present.
ladder_safety.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer the 4:1 angle, top securing, side-rail extension, ladder damage, or worker footing when those details are outside the image.
ladder_safety.consistency_rule: Do not call a tie-off, stabilizer, footing, handhold, landing extension, or ladder component absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

vehicle_backing.official_text: Motor vehicle equipment with an obstructed rear view may be used only with an audible reverse alarm or when backed up under an observer's signal; equipment near power lines has additional clearance requirements.
vehicle_backing.interpretation: Use narrowly for trucks, dump trucks, loaders, rollers, forklifts, and similar vehicles that are visibly reversing or whose rear path clearly contains a worker. Retrieval terms include backing, reverse, rear blind spot, truck, dump truck, loader, spotter, observer, alarm, and exclusion zone.
vehicle_backing.visual_trigger: A vehicle is visibly reversing, has reverse lights/clear backward operating context, or a worker is clearly standing in its immediate rear travel path or blind spot during active movement.
vehicle_backing.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project struck-by concern when active backing exposure is visually clear and the worker is in the rear danger zone without visible separation or a spotter. Do not infer the absence of a reverse alarm from a still image. A parked vehicle or a worker merely near equipment is not enough.
vehicle_backing.uncertainty_policy: If motion, rear travel direction, the worker's exact path, or separation control is unclear, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
vehicle_backing.consistency_rule: Do not call a spotter, barrier, exclusion zone, alarm, or separation control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

mobile_equipment_swing_radius.official_text: Construction equipment must be operated safely, and employers must instruct employees in recognizing and avoiding unsafe conditions.
mobile_equipment_swing_radius.interpretation: Dedicated card for excavator boom/arm/bucket swing, crane tail swing, backhoe movement, loader arm movement, and raised attachment strike zones. This fills the retrieval gap between backing, suspended-load, and falling-object cards.
mobile_equipment_swing_radius.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly within the apparent sweep, swing, strike, or crush path of an excavator boom, arm, bucket, counterweight, backhoe, loader arm, or similar mobile-equipment attachment during active work.
mobile_equipment_swing_radius.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project struck-by concern when the worker is visibly in the apparent swing/strike envelope and the image also shows active-operation context such as an operator, raised/extended attachment, digging/loading task, or movement-ready position. Do not require proof of motion from one frame. A clearly parked, lowered, non-operating machine near a worker is only Possible concern unless a direct danger-zone cue is visible.
mobile_equipment_swing_radius.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer speed, exact swing radius, machine motion, or operator awareness. If the worker is not clearly inside the path, report Possible concern rather than confirmation.
mobile_equipment_swing_radius.consistency_rule: Do not call a spotter, exclusion zone, barrier, operator, or equipment state absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

equipment_blind_spot_separation.official_text: Equipment and motor-vehicle rules require safe operation, including safeguards for obstructed rear views.
equipment_blind_spot_separation.interpretation: Use for a pedestrian worker close to the side, front, rear, or articulation zone of active heavy equipment even when the frame cannot prove reversing. It is a separation/danger-zone card, not a reverse-alarm card.
equipment_blind_spot_separation.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly close to active excavating, loading, hauling, compacting, or lifting equipment and no clearly marked pedestrian–equipment separation is visible.
equipment_blind_spot_separation.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project equipment-separation concern when the worker is inside an obvious equipment operating envelope or articulation/crush zone during active work and there is no visible separation control. Do not label it as a backing violation unless backing is actually visible.
equipment_blind_spot_separation.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer machine direction, alarm status, or exclusion-zone coverage beyond the visible scene. Use Possible concern if the equipment appears parked or the worker is clearly outside the operating envelope.
equipment_blind_spot_separation.consistency_rule: Do not call a barrier, spotter, marked route, cab operator, or exclusion zone absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

struck_by_falling_object.official_text: When employees are exposed to falling objects, employers must require hard hats and use measures such as toe-boards, screens, canopies, or barricades.
struck_by_falling_object.interpretation: Use for overhead work, objects/materials at a height over an occupied area, loose materials above workers, scaffold-edge debris, and falling-object exposure. It should not be used merely because a worker is outdoors.
struck_by_falling_object.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly under or immediately beside overhead work, a raised object/material, a scaffold edge with materials, an elevated bucket/load, or another concrete falling-object source.
struck_by_falling_object.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project falling-object concern when the worker and the overhead/falling-object source are both clear and the visible protection is absent or visibly inadequate. Do not require proof that the object is currently moving. If the source is merely stored safely or worker position is unclear, use Possible concern.
struck_by_falling_object.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer that an object will fall, that a source is unsecured, or that a worker is under it when depth/order cannot be established.
struck_by_falling_object.consistency_rule: Do not call a hard hat, toe-board, screen, canopy, barricade, or exclusion control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

suspended_load.official_text: Employees generally must be kept out of the fall zone of a suspended load and must not be directly under the load; limited essential-task exceptions apply.
suspended_load.interpretation: Use for cranes, hoists, lifting hooks, slings, rigging, concrete buckets, prefabricated elements, and visibly suspended loads. Distinguish a true suspended load from a boom or bucket resting on the ground.
suspended_load.visual_trigger: A crane, hoist, lifting device, hook, sling, or rigging visibly supports a load that is hanging above ground level while a worker is directly below or within the apparent fall zone.
suspended_load.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project suspended-load concern when the load is clearly suspended and a worker is directly under it or visibly within its fall zone without an evident essential load-handling task or exclusion control. Do not assume an essential-task exception from a still image; report it as a caveat if task context is unclear.
suspended_load.uncertainty_policy: If the load is not clearly suspended, the worker's location is unclear, or the worker may be performing an essential guiding/connection task, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
suspended_load.consistency_rule: Do not call a barricade, exclusion zone, tag line, rigger, or essential task absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

loading_unloading_falling_material.official_text: Employees must not be beneath loads handled by lifting or digging equipment and must stand away from vehicles being loaded or unloaded to avoid falling materials; haulage vehicles loaded by certain equipment need adequate cab protection for their operators.
loading_unloading_falling_material.interpretation: Use for trucks being loaded by excavators/loaders, workers standing beside a dumping/loading zone, loose material falling from a bucket, and people under a raised digging attachment. It complements but does not replace suspended-load retrieval.
loading_unloading_falling_material.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly beside, below, or in the immediate line of falling/spilling material from an excavator bucket, loader bucket, truck bed, crane load, or active loading/unloading operation.
loading_unloading_falling_material.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project struck-by concern when falling/spilling material or a raised loaded attachment is visibly over/adjacent to the worker and no clear separation is visible. A driver inside a visibly protected cab is not automatically a violation.
loading_unloading_falling_material.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer that a raised empty bucket contains material, that a truck is loading, or that a worker is outside protected cab space when the view is incomplete.
loading_unloading_falling_material.consistency_rule: Do not call a cab shield, barrier, separation zone, operator cab, or equipment state absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

excavation_safety.official_text: Employees in excavations must be protected from cave-ins by an adequate protective system unless the excavation is entirely stable rock or is less than 5 feet deep with a competent-person finding of no cave-in indication.
excavation_safety.interpretation: Primary trench/cave-in card for workers actually inside an excavation or trench. Retrieval terms include trench, excavation, trench box, shoring, shielding, sloping, benching, cave-in, vertical walls, and worker in trench.
excavation_safety.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly inside a trench, excavation, pit, or deep footing with potentially unstable sidewalls.
excavation_safety.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project cave-in concern when a worker is clearly inside a visibly deep, steep-sided, vertical, unsupported, or unprotected excavation and no shielding, shoring, sloping, or benching is visible. Do not drop a strong Pass 1 unsupported-trench observation simply because exact depth cannot be measured; explain that the 5-foot exception cannot be verified from the image. Use Possible concern only when the worker is not clearly inside the excavation or visible protection status is unclear.
excavation_safety.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer depth, soil classification, stable rock, competent-person inspection, or full protective-system coverage from a partial image.
excavation_safety.consistency_rule: Do not call sloping, benching, shoring, shielding, trench box, ladder, or protective system absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.official_text: Employees must be protected from materials or equipment that could fall or roll into excavations by keeping them at least 2 feet from the edge or using retaining devices.
excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.interpretation: Use for spoil piles, soil heaps, pipes, materials, equipment, buckets, and vehicles positioned at a trench edge above people inside the trench. It is specific to material rolling/falling into the excavation.
excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly inside or immediately below an excavation while spoil, materials, equipment, a vehicle, or a raised attachment is positioned at the excavation edge where it could fall or roll in.
excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project excavation falling-material concern when the worker is clearly in the excavation and the material/equipment is visibly at the lip or directly above the worker without a visible retaining control. Do not require an exact 2-foot measurement when the material is visibly at the edge; state that distance cannot be measured. Use Possible concern if relative position is ambiguous.
excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer hidden retaining devices, exact edge distance, soil stability, or whether material is secured.
excavation_spoil_pile_and_falling_materi.consistency_rule: Do not call a retaining device, barricade, stop log, trench box, or edge control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.official_text: When mobile equipment operates adjacent to or approaches an excavation edge without the operator having a clear direct view of the edge, a warning system such as barricades, signals, or stop logs must be used.
excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.interpretation: Use when excavators, trucks, loaders, or compactors work directly beside a trench/excavation edge. It separates equipment–trench collapse risk from general swing-radius risk.
excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.visual_trigger: Mobile equipment is visibly operated, positioned, or moving at the edge of a trench, excavation, pit, or embankment, particularly where a drop-off or unstable edge is visible.
excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project excavation-equipment concern when active mobile equipment is visibly at an excavation edge and no warning system, stop log, barricade, or signal arrangement is visible. Do not require proof that the operator lacks a full view; the card identifies a visible high-risk condition, not a final enforcement finding.
excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.uncertainty_policy: If equipment is parked well away from the edge, no excavation edge is visible, or a warning control may exist outside the frame, report Possible concern.
excavation_mobile_equipment_edge.consistency_rule: Do not call a barricade, stop log, signaler, spotter, or equipment position absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

caught_in_machinery.official_text: Belts, gears, shafts, pulleys, sprockets, spindles, drums, flywheels, chains, and other moving parts must be guarded where employees can contact them or where they create a hazard.
caught_in_machinery.interpretation: Use for saws, drills, mixers, conveyors, rollers, rotating shafts, belts, gears, pinch points, moving guards, and worker contact with machine operating zones.
caught_in_machinery.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly operating, cleaning, maintaining, reaching toward, or standing within contact distance of exposed moving/rotating parts, an in-going nip point, or a clear pinch/crush zone.
caught_in_machinery.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project caught-in concern when the unguarded hazardous part or pinch point is clearly visible and the worker's hands, body, clothing, or task places them in its exposure zone. Do not require visible motion if the machine is visibly being used or the worker is actively interacting with the hazard. A powered tool merely sitting on a surface is not enough.
caught_in_machinery.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer machine motion, guard removal, lockout status, or worker reachability when those are not visible.
caught_in_machinery.consistency_rule: Do not call a machine guard, barrier, interlock, separation device, or machine state absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

caught_between_equipment_and_structure.official_text: Equipment must be operated safely, and employers must instruct employees to recognize and avoid unsafe conditions.
caught_between_equipment_and_structure.interpretation: Use for workers caught/crushed between mobile equipment and a wall, truck, trench edge, stack, formwork, structural column, or other fixed object. This is a hazard-screening card rather than a one-image statutory determination.
caught_between_equipment_and_structure.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly standing, walking, guiding, or working in a narrow closing zone between mobile equipment/attachment and a fixed object or another vehicle.
caught_between_equipment_and_structure.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project caught-between concern when the worker is visibly in an obvious crush zone during active equipment operation or positioning and no separation control is visible. Do not require proof of actual impact or machine movement in one frame. A wide, clearly safe gap or parked equipment is not enough.
caught_between_equipment_and_structure.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer motion direction, exact clearance, equipment operator awareness, or actual contact. Use Possible concern when the gap or operating state is unclear.
caught_between_equipment_and_structure.consistency_rule: Do not call a spotter, barrier, exclusion zone, equipment state, or protected escape path absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

raised_equipment_maintenance.official_text: Heavy machinery, equipment, or parts suspended or held aloft by slings, hoists, or jacks must be substantially blocked or cribbed before employees work under or between them; buckets, blades, and dump bodies must be lowered or blocked when repaired or not in use.
raised_equipment_maintenance.interpretation: Use for mechanics or workers underneath a raised dump bed, raised loader bucket, bulldozer blade, excavator attachment, or jacked equipment. It is a high-value direct visual rule for caught-between hazards.
raised_equipment_maintenance.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly under, between, or reaching beneath a raised bucket, blade, dump body, vehicle, suspended machine part, or jacked equipment.
raised_equipment_maintenance.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project caught-between concern when the raised equipment part and worker exposure are clear and no blocking, cribbing, stand, or other support is visible. Do not assume hydraulic systems alone are adequate support.
raised_equipment_maintenance.uncertainty_policy: If the worker is not under/between the raised part, the part is fully lowered, or a support may be hidden, report Possible concern rather than confirming.
raised_equipment_maintenance.consistency_rule: Do not call a block, cribbing, jack stand, safety prop, or equipment support absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

electrical_safety.official_text: Employees may not work close enough to an electric power circuit to contact it unless protected by deenergizing/grounding or effective guarding, insulation, or other means; live parts must be guarded against accidental contact.
electrical_safety.interpretation: Broad electrical fallback card. Use only when a visible electrical source and a potentially exposed worker/task exist. More specific cards below should be preferred for exposed parts, damaged cords, open panels, and overhead power lines.
electrical_safety.visual_trigger: A visibly accessible electrical source is present: exposed conductor, open panel, damaged cable, temporary wiring, tool/cord defect, or overhead power line near a worker, metal object, crane, scaffold, or equipment.
electrical_safety.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project electrical-safety concern when Pass 1 clearly shows accessible electrical hazard evidence and a worker/tool/equipment is within a credible contact or approach path without visible guarding, insulation, separation, or deenergization evidence. Do not discard a clear exposed-wire or open-panel observation merely because voltage cannot be determined. Use Possible concern for source-only scenes with no exposed person/task.
electrical_safety.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer voltage, energization, grounding, circuit condition, qualifications, or contact potential from a still image. These unknowns affect legal certainty, not whether the visible hazard cue is retained.
electrical_safety.consistency_rule: Do not call insulation, guarding, lockout, deenergization, GFCI, distance control, or another protection measure absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

exposed_electrical_parts.official_text: Live parts of electrical equipment operating at 50 volts or more must be guarded against accidental contact; employees near electric circuits must be protected from shock by deenergizing, grounding, or effective guarding/insulation.
exposed_electrical_parts.interpretation: Use for open electrical panels, missing panel covers, exposed terminals, accessible conductors, open junction boxes, exposed busbars, bare live parts, and electric components accessible to workers.
exposed_electrical_parts.visual_trigger: An open panel, exposed terminal, bare conductor, open junction box, missing enclosure/cover, or another visibly accessible electrical part is present near a worker or accessible work area.
exposed_electrical_parts.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project electrical concern when the exposed part and credible worker access/contact path are both visible and no enclosure, guard, barrier, or separation is visible. Source-only images should be retained as Possible concern rather than discarded; they cannot establish worker exposure from the frame alone.
exposed_electrical_parts.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer energization, voltage, whether a panel is deenergized for service, or whether a qualified worker is controlling access.
exposed_electrical_parts.consistency_rule: Do not call a cover, lock, enclosure, barrier, insulation, warning sign, or access control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.official_text: Worn or frayed electric cords or cables shall not be used; construction temporary wiring has additional ground-fault and assured-equipment-grounding requirements.
damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.interpretation: Use for frayed cords, exposed conductor at a cable, taped/damaged extension cords, cords in standing water, crushed cables, damaged plugs, improvised temporary wiring, and cords creating a trip/electrical contact cue.
damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.visual_trigger: A cord, cable, plug, or temporary wiring connection is visibly frayed, cut, crushed, exposed, damaged, routed through water, or used in an obviously unsafe condition near a worker.
damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project electrical concern when visible cable/plug damage or water-contact exposure is clear and the cord is visibly in use, accessible, or within the worker path. Do not require proof that the circuit is energized. Do not treat an intact cord on dry ground as an electrical violation merely because it is visible.
damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer hidden internal conductor damage, GFCI presence, exact voltage, or whether a cord is currently energized from the image.
damaged_cords_temporary_wiring.consistency_rule: Do not call insulation, grounding, GFCI, cord protection, cable ramp, or equipment state absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

overhead_power_lines.official_text: For crane/equipment operations near power lines, the regulations require specified clearance and protective measures; under 29 CFR 1926.600, overhead wires are treated as energized unless confirmed otherwise and visibly grounded.
overhead_power_lines.interpretation: Use for cranes, booms, excavators, loaders, scaffold components, long metal objects, ladders, or workers operating near visible overhead electrical lines. This is separate from open-panel/exposed-wire rules.
overhead_power_lines.visual_trigger: An overhead power line is visibly near a crane, boom, raised equipment, scaffold, ladder, long conductive object, or worker performing a task that could bring them into contact/approach.
overhead_power_lines.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project overhead-line concern when the image clearly shows equipment, load, scaffold, ladder, or a conductive object operating in the apparent line-clearance envelope with no visible separation/spotter/barrier. Do not require exact voltage or a tape-measure distance to retain a clearly close approach cue; report exact legal clearance as Not assessable when not measurable.
overhead_power_lines.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer voltage, line energization status, exact clearance distance, grounding, or utility coordination. A distant line with no plausible approach path is not enough.
overhead_power_lines.consistency_rule: Do not call a spotter, insulating barrier, warning device, deenergization, grounding, or clearance control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

head_protection.official_text: Employees working where there is possible danger of head injury from impact, falling/flying objects, or electrical shock and burns must be protected by helmets; PPE must be provided and used where hazards can cause injury.
head_protection.interpretation: Use for hard hat / protective helmet assessment. For this project, active-construction context is a valid operational trigger because datasets and site safety programs commonly label uncovered heads in active work areas as PPE non-compliance even when a single image cannot isolate one discrete falling-object source.
head_protection.visual_trigger: A worker is clearly within active construction work or a construction hazard context—such as excavation, formwork, rebar, structural work, scaffolding, elevated work, demolition, material handling, overhead work, heavy equipment operation, or electrical work—and the head is visible enough to assess a helmet.
head_protection.confirmation_threshold: For this project's image-grounded PPE screening, confirm a hard-hat non-compliance concern when a worker is clearly in active construction context and the helmet is explicitly Not visible. Do not require Pass 1 to prove one separate falling-object source before retaining the finding. For strict statutory OSHA wording, note that the exact head-injury exposure may require site context; this caveat must not silently downgrade the project PPE concern.
head_protection.uncertainty_policy: If the person may be a visitor, the activity/site context is not active construction, the head is occluded, or helmet visibility is Unclear, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
head_protection.consistency_rule: Do not call a hard hat/helmet absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.
head_protection.source_type: OSHA-derived + project operational PPE screening rule

high_visibility_traffic_exposure.official_text: Employees exposed to public vehicular traffic must wear warning vests or other reflectorized/high-visibility garments; flagger warning garments must conform to MUTCD requirements.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.interpretation: Use for high-visibility vests, reflective garments, hi-vis clothing, flaggers, road work, traffic control, trucks, loaders, excavators, haul roads, and workers exposed to vehicle or equipment traffic. It supplies the missing hi-vis retrieval target.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly exposed to public traffic, haul-road traffic, active vehicles, mobile plant, loading/unloading traffic, or performs a flagging/traffic-control role, and the torso is visible enough to assess hi-vis clothing.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a high-visibility PPE concern when the worker is clearly in traffic or active mobile-equipment exposure and hi-vis clothing is explicitly Not visible. Treat it as a confirmed OSHA-specific issue when public-traffic exposure or a flagger role is visible. For internal site plant traffic without public traffic, retain it as a confirmed project PPE concern and state that the exact statutory hi-vis scope may require site context.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.uncertainty_policy: Do not infer traffic exposure merely because a worker is outdoors, or infer absence when the torso is covered, obstructed, or image quality is too poor. If vehicles are parked/non-operational, use Possible concern unless a clear traffic route/exposure remains visible.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.consistency_rule: Do not call a high-visibility vest, reflective garment, traffic barrier, spotter, or separation control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.
high_visibility_traffic_exposure.source_type: OSHA-derived + project operational PPE screening rule

eye_face_protection.official_text: Affected employees must use appropriate eye or face protection when exposed to flying particles, molten metal, chemicals, gases/vapors, or injurious light radiation.
eye_face_protection.interpretation: Use for cutting, grinding, drilling, welding, chipping, demolition dust/particles, chemical splashes, spray application, and other direct eye/face-hazard tasks.
eye_face_protection.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly performing or immediately adjacent to an active task that produces flying particles, sparks, molten metal, chemical splash, vapor, or bright welding radiation, and the face/eyes are visible enough to assess protection.
eye_face_protection.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project eye/face PPE concern when an active eye/face-hazard task is clear and the required goggles, safety glasses, face shield, or welding shield is explicitly Not visible. Do not require a visible injury, sparks in the exact frame, or a product label. A worker standing near inactive tools is not enough.
eye_face_protection.uncertainty_policy: If the task is paused, protection may be hidden by angle, or the worker is not clearly exposed, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
eye_face_protection.consistency_rule: Do not call safety glasses, goggles, face shield, welding helmet, or other eye/face protection absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.

hand_protection.official_text: Appropriate PPE must be provided and used where process, environmental, chemical, or mechanical hazards can injure the body or extremities.
hand_protection.interpretation: Use for handling sharp edges, rebar, glass, sheet metal, abrasive materials, hot material, chemicals, wet concrete, energized components, or tools/tasks creating a clear hand-contact hazard.
hand_protection.visual_trigger: A worker's hand is visibly handling or immediately contacting a sharp, hot, chemical, abrasive, energized, pinch-point, or other obvious hand hazard, and the hands are visible enough to assess gloves.
hand_protection.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project hand-protection concern when active hand exposure is clear and gloves are explicitly Not visible. Do not require generic gloves for a worker whose task has no visible hand hazard. Do not infer that gloves are unsuitable merely by color or style.
hand_protection.uncertainty_policy: If hands are behind material, gloves may be occluded, or the task/hazard is unclear, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
hand_protection.consistency_rule: Do not call gloves absent when Pass 1 records them as Visible or Unclear.

foot_protection.official_text: Appropriate protective equipment for extremities must be used where hazards can cause injury; protective footwear is required where foot injury hazards are present.
foot_protection.interpretation: Use for crush hazards from materials/equipment, puncture hazards from nails/rebar/scrap, hot/corrosive materials, wet concrete, or visibly unsafe footwear in an active foot-exposure task. This card is intentionally conservative because footwear is often too small to inspect accurately.
foot_protection.visual_trigger: A worker's feet are clearly visible in an active foot-hazard context involving heavy materials, equipment movement, sharp debris, protruding rebar/nails, hot/wet/corrosive material, or other direct foot exposure.
foot_protection.confirmation_threshold: Confirm a project foot-protection concern only when the task hazard and visibly inadequate footwear are both clear (for example, open footwear in a direct construction foot-hazard task). Do not confirm merely because safety-toe features cannot be seen; normal closed boots cannot be verified from an image.
foot_protection.uncertainty_policy: If footwear type, toe protection, task hazard, or foot visibility is unclear, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable.
foot_protection.consistency_rule: Do not call boots, safety footwear, toe protection, gaiters, or foot controls absent when Pass 1 records them as Visible or Unclear.

respiratory_protection.official_text: Construction respiratory-protection requirements are the same as 29 CFR 1910.134, which depends on exposure assessment, contaminant, controls, and respirator selection.
respiratory_protection.interpretation: Use for visible dust clouds, silica-producing cutting/grinding, fumes, smoke, spray paint mist, chemical vapor, welding fume, confined-space atmospheric exposure, and respiratory devices.
respiratory_protection.visual_trigger: A worker is visibly within a dust cloud, fume/smoke plume, spray mist, chemical vapor, or another clearly visible airborne contaminant while performing or standing beside the generating task.
respiratory_protection.confirmation_threshold: Retain a visible airborne-exposure cue as a respiratory-protection concern. Confirm a project PPE concern only when airborne exposure is clear and a bare face/no respiratory protection is explicitly visible in a task that obviously generates substantial dust/fume/mist. Do not claim a final OSHA respiratory violation from a single image, because concentration, duration, control effectiveness, and respirator selection cannot be determined.
respiratory_protection.uncertainty_policy: If the contaminant, exposure duration, face visibility, or local ventilation/control is unclear, report Possible concern and compliance Not assessable rather than dropping the cue.
respiratory_protection.consistency_rule: Do not call a respirator, local exhaust, wet-cutting control, ventilation, or other exposure control absent when Pass 1 records it as Visible or Unclear.
